canonical_name: International Summer School for Young Physicists (ISSYP)
organization: Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, Canada
why_it_was_a_candidate: On paper an excellent fit — a genuine theoretical-physics programme at a world-class institute, historically open to international students, and exactly the kind of research-adjacent opportunity ORYN's corpus lacks. I was actively preparing to add it.
evidence: Perimeter's own ISSYP page states: 'The International Summer School for Young Physicists (ISSYP) program will not be offered in 2024.'
how_i_verified_it_independently: `oryn-ce` reported this before their lane closed and I said I would confirm it from the source rather than take their label — the same discipline I have applied to my own claims all night. Direct retrieval failed three ways: WebFetch got HTTP 403, the real Browser pane got '403 Access Denied', and web.archive.org is blocked in this environment. So I confirmed it a fourth way — a search engine's own crawl of perimeterinstitute.ca/issyp surfaces the same sentence. That is an INDEPENDENT crawler reading the same official page and finding the same text `oryn-ce`'s agent quoted.
the_403_is_not_evidence_about_the_progra: Worth stating plainly: perimeterinstitute.ca returns 403 to WebFetch, to a real browser, and (per oryn-ce) to Internet Archive crawlers on four separate dates. That is a server-side block on automated access, NOT a dead site and NOT a signal about the programme. Conflating 'I got a 403' with 'this no longer exists' is exactly the error that would have made this record wrong in the other direction.
THE_LIMIT_OF_WHAT_I_ESTABLISHED: The quoted sentence is about **2024**. It is now 2026. I could NOT read the current page, so I cannot tell whether ISSYP has since resumed, been formally discontinued, or simply not been updated. What is established: as of the indexed version of Perimeter's own page, ISSYP was not running in 2024, and there is no evidence of a later edition. What is NOT established: that it is permanently ended.
recommendation: Do not add to the corpus. Revisit only if Perimeter publishes a new edition. If it is ever added, it must NOT be added on the strength of historical descriptions of the programme — several third-party sites still describe ISSYP in the present tense.
confidence_reason: High confidence in the 2024 non-offering; medium overall because I could not read the live page to check for anything after 2024.
credit: Finding originated with oryn-ce; independently re-verified here by a different route.

why_it_was_a_candidate: A search result described it as 'a global, fully virtual innovation and problem-solving competition for high school students (ages 13-18)' — which would have been an excellent fit: global, virtual, free of travel, and squarely in the Design/Entrepreneurship interests my gap analysis (CR1-152) found thin.
verdict: DO NOT ADD — could not be found on the operator's own site.
what_i_actually_found: Searching lse.ac.uk directly returns LSE Generate's Schools Programme and a five-day **Innovation Bootcamp** at LSE for 15-19 year olds. No page for a 'Global Innovation Challenge' or 'LGIC' surfaced on the LSE domain at all. The bootcamp is a short in-person programme, not a global virtual competition, and by its nature is a summer programme — outside my scope and a different thing entirely from what was described.
the_pattern_this_illustrates: This is aggregator inflation: a real institution (LSE), a real adjacent programme (the Schools Programme / Innovation Bootcamp), and a plausible-sounding competition name attached to them that the institution itself does not publish. Same family as the Blackstone case (CR1-151), where a search result implied a Cambridge affiliation the operator explicitly denies — except here the entity may not exist under that name at all.
why_recording_a_negative_matters_here: Without this note the next researcher hits the same aggregator description, finds it plausible, and either adds an unverifiable row or spends the same time rediscovering that LSE does not publish it. 'Searched the operator's own domain and it is not there' is a finding.
honest_limit: I searched lse.ac.uk via three query formulations. I did NOT exhaustively crawl the site, and info.lse.ac.uk is a large estate. So the correct statement is 'not found on the operator's domain', not 'does not exist'. If someone produces an LSE-hosted page for it, that supersedes this note immediately.
